title: Adverse Adolescent Experiences and Feelings of Hopelessness in Chicago’s Southside: The Protective Role of Creative Expression
abstract: This study examined the association between adverse adolescent experiences (AAEs) and feelings of hopelessness, as well as creative expression’s potential to moderate feelings of hopelessness among African American youth. Data were provided by 131 African American youths (ages 13–24) and their caregivers residing in Chicago’s Southside. Self-reports on 17 AAEs captured household dysfunction and peer victimization. Linear regression analyses examined the associations between AAE exposure (yes/no), total AAE burden, and latent AAE classes and hopelessness. Creative expressions (e.g., writing poems, songs, or rap, or writing in a journal or notebook) were examined as a moderator of these associations. AAEs prevalence ranged from 27.5% to 58.8%. AAEs were associated with greater hopelessness, whereas creative expression was associated with lower hopelessness. Moderation analyses showed that creative expression significantly attenuated the positive association between AAEs and hopelessness. Encouraging creative expression may aid in reducing youths’ feelings of hopelessness in the face of adverse experiences.
